concept.name: Zero-CPU Tab Controls and Hover Previews Excision
concept.description: Replacing tab bar SVG elements with unicode characters, purging website favicons to reduce image decoding, and disabling layout-heavy tab hover previews.
concept.content:
To achieve true zero-CPU performance in the Firefox interface on legacy hardware (Intel HD 4000), we applied the following surgical updates to the theme and configurations:
1. Tab Close Button (SVG Excision): - Hides the native SVG-based close button (`.tab-close-button > .toolbarbutton-icon`). - Converts the parent button container `.tab-close-button` into a flex container and injects a raw monospace text glyph `content: "×"`. - This avoids XML parsing, Skia vector path evaluation, and VRAM texture upload thrashing for close buttons on tab hover.
2. Website Favicon Purge: - Hides the `.tab-icon-image`, `.tab-sharing-icon-overlay`, and `.tab-icon-overlay` elements. - This eliminates runtime CPU paint cycles and texture updates when tabs load or change website favicons (e.g. Google, GitHub logos).
3. Text-Based Navigation Controls: - Replaces standard SVG icons for Back, Forward, Reload/Stop, and Home buttons with lightweight unicode character labels (`<`, `>`, `↻`, `X`, `H`).
4. Tab Hover Previews Excision: - Disables the heavy layout and thumbnail generation engine for tab cards. - Configuration settings updated to false: - `browser.tabs.hoverPreview.enabled` - `browser.tabs.hoverPreview.showThumbnails` - `browser.tabs.groups.hoverPreview.enabled` - JS Modification: Patched `browser/components/tabbrowser/content/tab.js` mouse enter/leave listeners to prevent dispatching the custom XUL events (`TabHoverStart` and `TabHoverEnd`) if the preference is disabled. This stops event creation, object allocation, and DOM bubbling overhead on mouse movement.
